seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Estes Park, CO 2026
seo_desc: Christmas events for kids in Estes Park, Colorado for 2026: the Catch the Glow Parade, Santa visits, lights, free movies and more, with dates checked.
lede: Estes Park lights up Elkhorn Avenue with the Catch the Glow Parade the day after Thanksgiving, then adds glowing wildlife in Bond Park, Santa visits and free holiday movies.
celebrates: The Town of Estes Park's events team anchors the season with the Catch the Glow Parade on Elkhorn Avenue, where more than 40 entries, including floats from the Town and local nonprofits, marching bands and fire trucks, roll past as many as 30,000 spectators. Visit Estes Park adds a new set of lights in Bond Park, with 11 illuminated wildlife decorations, plus lights along Moraine Avenue and Cleave Street. Local businesses join in with a Snowman Scavenger Hunt, free movies at the Historic Park Theatre and Santa visits across town, so families can spread the fun over several weekends in the mountains.
lastyear: Last year the Catch the Glow Parade took place on Friday, November 28, 2025, and Estes Park News called it one of the town's signature events. A local recap of the Lighting of the Trees described festivities starting at 3:30 pm with hot chocolate, candy canes, ornament making, carolers, carriage rides and an all ages electric train. The Rocky Mountain Channel's recap video of the 2025 parade shows colorful floats, music and appearances by Santa and Mrs. Claus, which gives families a good idea of what the evening looks like.
facts: The Catch the Glow Parade happens the day after Thanksgiving, and the Town says up to 30,000 spectators gather along Elkhorn Avenue for it. The Stanley Chocolate Factory sits at 157 West Elkhorn Avenue and lets children make their own chocolate bar or ride its carousel, which has a 42 inch height requirement. The Stanley Hotel hosts Boulder Ballet's Nutcracker Suite with Santa photos in the Pavilion before each show, and the Historic Park Theatre screens free holiday movies on Saturday mornings.
trains: We did not find a Christmas train ride in Estes Park for 2026, so families who want rails and lights have a couple of options nearby. Last year's Lighting of the Trees in Estes Park included an all ages electric train, according to a local recap, and the Rocky Mountain Train Show brings model and toy trains to The Ranch Events Complex in Loveland on November 28 and 29. Check each host's site for current details before you travel from Estes Park.
traditions: A lighted parade down Elkhorn Avenue the day after Thanksgiving with floats, marching bands and fire trucks.
A community event with festive music and twinkling lights that opens the holiday season.
A nightly light display with 11 illuminated wildlife decorations, from bears to owls.
Children collect stamps from hidden snowmen in downtown shops and can earn a free ornament.
The Historic Park Theatre shows free holiday films on Saturday mornings, paid for by local businesses.
Santa visits the Stanley Chocolate Factory, the YMCA of the Rockies, the Visitor Center and more.
kidfact: Estes Park lights up 11 wildlife decorations in Bond Park, including bears, elk, foxes, owls, rabbits and squirrels, so children can pick a glowing favorite.
faq: How does Estes Park celebrate Christmas?

The town holds the free Catch the Glow Parade on Elkhorn Avenue the day after Thanksgiving, lights Bond Park and downtown streets, and runs a Snowman Scavenger Hunt. Local venues add Santa visits, free Saturday movies at the Historic Park Theatre and holiday shows such as the Boulder Ballet Nutcracker Suite at The Stanley Hotel.
Is the Catch the Glow Parade free?

Yes. The Town of Estes Park lists the parade as a free event on Elkhorn Avenue. It takes place the day after Thanksgiving at 5:30 pm, and the Town says up to 30,000 spectators come to watch more than 40 entries, so it is smart to arrive early and bring warm layers.
Where can kids meet Santa in Estes Park?

Visit Estes Park lists Santa at the Stanley Chocolate Factory, the YMCA of the Rockies, the Estes Park Visitor Center and Cookies with Santa at Black Canyon Inn. Santa also rides in the Catch the Glow Parade. Each host sets its own dates, so check the listing for the day you plan to visit.
Is there a free holiday activity in Estes Park for children?

Yes. The Snowman Scavenger Hunt is free, with punch cards at the Visitor Center and participating shops. The Historic Park Theatre shows free holiday movies on selected Saturdays, the Bond Park lights are free to see, and the Festival of Trees at The Estes Park Resort is free to enter.
What should we wear to Christmas events in Estes Park?

Visit Estes Park suggests packing an extra layer for children who stand outside after dark, and ear protection for little ones sensitive to band noise at the parade. The town sits in the mountains, so evenings in late November and December are cold.
